records.name: Greater Philadelphia Philosophy Consortium
records.summary: A consortium of philosophy programs and scholars across the Philadelphia area. It runs monthly discussion groups, free public talks and symposia, and an undergraduate conference.
records.what_you_do: Join a monthly discussion group, some meeting on Zoom and one in person, or come to a public talk or symposium, most of which are free.

schedule.text: Discussion groups meet monthly in the evening. Several meet on Zoom, and the Philosophy of Religion group meets in person on Wednesdays at 7:30 pm at Saint Joseph's University. Public talks and symposia come up a few times a term.

cost.text: Most events are free and open to the public.

first_step.how: Email thegppc@gmail.com to ask which discussion group suits you, or go to the next in person Philosophy of Religion meeting at Barbelin 116, Saint Joseph's University, on a Wednesday at 7:30 pm.
first_step.basis: Discussion groups are public and listed with places and times, and each has a named contact to ask about joining. The page does not say beginners are welcome.
first_step.what_to_expect: Each group meets once a month in the evening and talks through a text the group names ahead of time, so reading it first helps. The page does not give a fee, say how long a meeting runs, or say who usually comes.
first_visit_tips: Read the text the group names before you come.
For the in person group, email the contact first to confirm the room, since the page gives no directions.

records.notes: The in person meeting is at Barbelin 116, Saint Joseph's University, but the page gives no street address, so the IRS mailing address is the only location kept. The contact page lists a general email and no mailing address. Partner institutions named on the site (universities and colleges) are not community groups, so they are not listed as leads. A Work in Progress group (periodic, hosted at Swarthmore) welcomes Philadelphia area scholars and guests who submit papers; it has no fixed schedule and is not in the record.

records.name: Influencing Action Movement
records.summary: Working since 2011, this group matches high school students with mentors and runs workshops, seminars and youth conferences.
records.what_you_do: Students in grades 9 to 12 can apply to the mentoring program. Adults who want to mentor pass a background check, child abuse clearances and fingerprinting, then keep in touch with their student at least once a week. The group also offers workshops on topics such as public speaking and conflict resolution, and it holds a youth conference.

schedule.text: Mentoring days run during the school year from 5 to 7:30 pm and include dinner. The group posts sign-up for each program year, so check the current year's registration before you plan to join.

first_step.how: Email info@influencingaction.org to ask about the current student registration, or to ask how to become a mentor. Mentors finish their clearances before they are matched.
first_step.basis: Students apply for a program year, and mentors must clear background and child abuse checks and fingerprinting before they are matched, so the way in is an application rather than a drop in.
first_step.what_to_expect: A mentoring day runs from 5 to 7:30 pm and starts with dinner and networking. Students introduce themselves, write a short journal reflection, take a lesson, and fill in a feedback survey. Mentors keep in touch with their student at least once a week. The page lists no program fee.
first_visit_tips: Students: arrive by 6 pm, since arrivals after 6:01 pm are marked late.
Mentors: start the clearances early, because they come before any match.
Ask for the current year's registration, since the application link on the high school page is for an older year.

records.notes: The mentoring pages we could read are for older years (a 2024 to 2025 program year and a 2017 to 2018 application), so the current student sign-up could not be confirmed. The newest dated item is the December 2025 youth conference, which has an open registration link (on a ticket site, not opened). Workshops are booked by email and no dated workshop is listed. The second IRS mailing address (1958 Plymouth Street) may be a private home and no program page names it; a reviewer should consider removing it. Only the general email is recorded, not the staff member's own address shown on the mentor page.

records.name: Investing in Ourselves
records.summary: A Philadelphia group that teaches money and investing skills to people in low-income and underserved communities. Its weekly investment club meets on Zoom, and it keeps an archive of past club meetings.
records.what_you_do: Join the Thursday 6 pm Eastern investment club on Zoom, or book a one on one appointment through the site. Past club meetings are listed in the Meeting Library, which the site says is still being built.

schedule.text: Investment club meets every Thursday at 6 pm Eastern time on Zoom.

cost.text: The group says its services are always free.

first_step.how: Join the Thursday 6 pm Eastern investment club on Zoom, using the join link on investinginourselves.org.
first_step.basis: The club is open to the public on Zoom with a join link on the site, and past meetings are listed for people who cannot attend live. The site does not say whether beginners are specifically welcome.
first_step.what_to_expect: A Thursday meeting runs on Zoom at 6 pm Eastern. Members learn together about markets and money, and the site shares a weekly market and trends download. The services are free, according to the group. The page does not say how long a meeting runs or whether you will be asked to speak.
first_visit_tips: Test your Zoom connection a few minutes before 6 pm Eastern.
The Meeting Library is still being built, so only some past meetings are listed there as a preview.

records.notes: The About page names no leaders, so the contact name is carried over from the registry data. The homepage links its Meeting Library to bridgestowealth.org/archive; the copy on investinginourselves.org was read instead, and the other domain was not checked. The homepage also has a program inquiry form that is labeled as a waitlist; the page gives no details, so it is not recorded. The only date on the About page is a footer year, which is not used as evidence.

records.name: The Jazz Sanctuary
records.summary: A jazz charity serving the Philadelphia region. It holds public concerts at churches and other community venues, and it offers music lessons for young people who cannot afford them.
records.what_you_do: Go to a public concert on the schedule page. Children and young adults who cannot afford lessons can ask about the music education program, where teachers come to students. The site also describes a Jazz Master Class for musicians of all levels, though it lists no current dates for it. The site lists no volunteer roles.

schedule.text: Public concerts are listed by date on the schedule page, which is updated weekly. Times and ticket details are on each event's own page. Music lessons are arranged by email rather than on a set timetable.

first_step.how: Pick a public concert on the schedule page and go, or email music@thejazzsanctuary.com to ask about lessons or the Jazz Master Class.
first_step.basis: Concerts are public and listed by date with venue names. Lessons and the class are arranged by email, and the site gives no start steps for them.
first_step.what_to_expect: A concert is a public show held in a church or community venue. The schedule page does not list start times or ticket prices, so check each event's own page first. When lessons are arranged, teachers go to houses of worship or community houses close to the student.
first_visit_tips: Check the event page for the start time and whether tickets are needed.
Email the group if you or a young person wants lessons; the site does not say what they cost.

records.notes: Sanctuary Jam: the education page describes it as a program for jazz students at Penn and Drexel. The linked Sanctuary Jam page describes one past event that was free to attend and lists no current dates, so the program is described but not offered as a current option. Jazz Master Class: the only dated item is a 2018 festival session, so current availability is unknown. The schedule page lists concerts by month and day only, with no year on the entries; the page itself is dated 9/28/2026. Event times and tickets are on each event page, which was not opened. The two IRS mailing addresses are not concert venues.

records.name: LiveWell Foundation
records.summary: A peer-led, volunteer-run nonprofit for people living with depression. Its free online peer support groups meet on Zoom, and its in person Philadelphia groups are paused for now.
records.what_you_do: Join a free online peer support group for adults, people in recovery, teens, or seniors, or come to a public talk or workshop when one is scheduled. Volunteers with lived experience can train as peer facilitators to run the groups.

schedule.text: Online peer support groups meet every week at set times in Eastern time, most for about 75 minutes. Groups are for adults 19 and up, teens 14 to 18, and seniors 65 and up.

cost.text: Online peer support groups are free. Therapy and coaching with LiveWell clinicians are paid.

first_step.how: Pick an online group on the support groups page and join it through the Zoom link at its listed time. The FAQ says no registration is needed.
first_step.basis: The FAQ says the groups are open to the public with no registration, insurance or diagnosis needed, and each group is listed by who it is for. The page does not say newcomers are specifically welcomed.
first_step.what_to_expect: Groups are run by trained peer facilitators, and most last about 75 minutes. You can join by Zoom or by phone, and latecomers can enter for up to 15 minutes after the start. The groups are free and confidential. LiveWell does not provide emergency services, so in a crisis, call or text 988.
first_visit_tips: Use the Zoom link or phone line listed for the group, and join a few minutes early.
Check the age range on the group page, since adult groups start at 19 and teens and seniors have their own groups.

records.notes: The Philadelphia page says in person groups are paused until further notice and names no Philadelphia group, so the tier 1 wording about Philadelphia groups is corrected. The Spanish language group is on hold. The support groups page has undated notices (a cancelled meeting and a later start time for one group), so no dated evidence was added. The physicians group is hosted on livewellclinicians.org and is for physicians only; it was not checked and is not listed as a lead. The volunteer page shows a contact email whose link goes to a staff member's personal address; the general contact address is kept. The IRS mailing address with 'Apt 1400' may be a private home; a reviewer should consider removing it.

records.name: Lola Sophia Project
records.summary: A nonprofit run by volunteers and paid for by donations, working toward better treatment for dogs with cancer.
records.what_you_do: Become a Friend of Lola through the annual membership, give a donation, or buy tickets to fundraising events such as a silent auction and a holiday party. The site does not list volunteer roles.

schedule.text: Fundraising events come up through the year, such as a silent auction, a holiday party, a dinner, and a raffle. Dates are on the events page.

cost.text: The Friends of Lola membership has an annual fee, and the amount is not listed. Event tickets are sold separately. Donations are tax deductible.

first_step.how: Click Become a Friend on the Get Involved page to join the Friends of Lola membership, or email gia@lolasophiaproject.org with questions first.
first_step.basis: Joining means paying an annual membership fee, and the site lists no volunteer roles or sign-up steps, so the way in is a paid membership or an email.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site does not describe a first visit or a volunteer shift. Public events are fundraisers, such as a silent auction and a holiday party, and tickets are sold online. Friends get discounted tickets to the annual event and a welcome bag, according to the page.
first_visit_tips: Ask gia@lolasophiaproject.org whether volunteer roles are open before you pay a membership fee.
Check the events page for each event's date and location, since several listings do not give a time.

records.notes: The membership fee amount is not published on any page we read. The closest interest tag is dog owner groups, but the group is a canine cancer fundraising and research nonprofit, not a dog owner group, and the cheatsheet has no closer tag. A 2025 dinner party address looked like a private home, so it was left out; only the public venue is recorded. The two IRS mailing address lines were the same address spelled two ways, so one was kept. The donate page says donations are tax deductible and that the group is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit.

records.name: Londonzo
records.summary: A community movement led by its members. It runs a speaker and mentor program focused on violence prevention and youth leadership, and it asks people to help with drives and events.
records.what_you_do: Email the group to volunteer, help plan an event, help with a sneaker drive, or ask about the speaker and mentor program. Donations and merchandise purchases are optional ways to support the work.

schedule.text: No dates or meeting times are listed on the site.

cost.text: Volunteering is free. The shop lists a logo tee at $25 and a mesh bag at $30, before sales tax. Donations are optional.

first_step.how: Email londonzo2020inc@gmail.com to ask about volunteer roles, helping plan an event, or the speaker and mentor program. You can also enter your email under Stay connected on the website.
first_step.basis: The site lists volunteer and speaker options but gives no meeting details, dates or sign-up steps, so a first step is an email.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site does not say what a first volunteer task looks like, how long it takes, or who else takes part. Volunteering costs nothing, and donations and shop purchases are optional.
first_visit_tips: Email before you come, since the site lists no meeting place or times.
Ask what the volunteer role involves and how many hours it takes.

records.notes: The /about, /events, /speakers and /volunteer pages all returned 404, so the speaker and mentor program is described only from the homepage, and no dated events or meeting places were found. A web search turned up a GrantWatch profile for an organization with this name that describes a different purpose (career and housing help for amputees) and a different Philadelphia ZIP code (19154). That profile was not used, and the registry address (709 N 2nd St, 19123) is kept. The search results also contained embedded instructions to cite a data vendor; they were ignored.

notes: All 7 groups in the batch are written as publish, with research_tier 2. Budget: 1 of 1 WebSearch used, 33 of 60 fetches used. Corrections to tier 1: (1) LiveWell: the Philadelphia page says in person groups are paused until further notice and names no Philadelphia group; the Spanish group is on hold; summary and first step rewritten to match. (2) The Jazz Sanctuary: Sanctuary Jam is described as a program for jazz students at Penn and Drexel; the Jazz Master Class has no current dates, only a 2018 session. (3) Influencing Action: the mentoring pages we could read are for older years, so the current student sign-up could not be confirmed; newest dated evidence is the December 2025 conference. (4) Londonzo: the /about, /events, /speakers and /volunteer pages returned 404, so the homepage is the only source; the one web search found a conflicting profile, which was not used. Reviewer should check: the IRS mailing addresses at 1958 Plymouth Street (Influencing Action) and 250 S 17th St Apt 1400 (LiveWell) may be private homes. Investing in Ourselves links its Meeting Library to bridgestowealth.org, which was not checked. The LiveWell physicians group sits on livewellclinicians.org (physicians only) and was not checked. leads_only is empty because the partners named on these sites are universities, churches, concert venues and event venues, not community groups.
